items.prompt:
A wave that bounces back off a material is:
A) Absorbed
B) Reflected
C) Transmitted
D) Created

A wave that passes through a material is:
A) Reflected
B) Absorbed
C) Transmitted
D) Destroyed

A wave whose energy is taken in by a material is:
A) Reflected
B) Absorbed
C) Transmitted
D) Doubled

steps: Taking in the energy is absorption.

items.prompt:
Light passing through a clear glass window is an example of:
A) Reflection
B) Absorption
C) Transmission
D) An echo

steps: Light passing through the glass is transmission.

items.prompt:
A dark shirt warming in sunlight shows light being:
A) Reflected
B) Absorbed
C) Transmitted
D) Ignored

steps: The shirt absorbs the light energy and warms up.

items.prompt:
An echo is an example of sound being:
A) Absorbed
B) Reflected
C) Transmitted
D) Created

Foam panels are used to quiet a recording studio because they:
A) Reflect sound
B) Absorb sound energy
C) Transmit all sound
D) Create new sound

steps: Soft foam absorbs sound waves, reducing echoes.

items.prompt:
Which statement is correct about how waves meet materials?
A) Only one interaction can ever happen
B) A wave may be reflected, absorbed, and transmitted at the same time
C) Waves always pass straight through
D) Waves never reflect
items.answer: B) A wave may be reflected, absorbed, and transmitted at the same time

steps: Multiple interactions can occur at once when a wave meets a material.
